 InFocus: Is adopting permanent daylight saving time a mistake?
 By Cierra Bettens 
 -->
 Nov 16, 2026 
 InFocus and the debate over changing the clock. 
 Many of us know how we feel when it’s time to change our clocks back in the fall and forward in the spring. Sleepy – maybe even a little disoriented.
 Well, on Nov. 1, citizens in six provinces and territories didn’t experience any of that because their governments scrapped the dreaded seasonal time change.
 Governments had two choices: stick with standard time or daylight saving time. Standard time gives you more sun in the morning – while daylight time gives you extended sun in the evening.
 Most chose to extend daylight into the evening.
 But will they regret their decision?
 This week on InFocus, David Prerau, one of the world’s foremost experts on daylight saving time, explains why they might.
 “What happened in the U.S. anyway is nobody was much against it until it actually occurred in January 1974,” Prerau, the author of Seize the Daylight, told host Cierra Bettens. “We had an incident in 1974 where there was an energy crisis, an unexpected energy crisis. And so they put in daylight saving time year-round for a two-year period, which they thought would cover the energy crisis. And most people thought it would be good until it happened.
 “Everybody saw they had to get up in the pitch dark, go to work in the pitch dark, and most people thought the worst thing was that to send their kids to school in the dark, walking on dark city streets or waiting at the bus stop on dark country roads. And so it lost popularity very quickly in the US, and I think 1974 and even though it was only a two-year plan, they got rid of it after one year because it was so unpopular.”
 Anishinaabe health scholar, Dr. Amy Shawanda, said if the government wants to adopt one particular time, she supports standard time. But she added, there are impacts of changing the clocks.
 “It’s not natural to our circadian rhythms,” she said. “A lot of people will feel off when the clocks change because it’s not natural to our circadian rhythms. As Indigenous Peoples, we never had to change the clocks. We just lived on the land, and so it’s not natural to who we are.
 “We should really move away from the daylight saving time and not adopt it at all, because it does really go against our own circadian rhythms. It goes against our biology.”
 Cierra Bettens 
 Host/Producer | Montréal Cierra is the host and co-producer of the of the weekly APTN News InFocus podcast. She joined APTN in 2024 as a reporter-correspondent in Winnipeg after working in campus and city news. She’s currently completing her Master of Arts in Media Studies at Concordia University in Montréal. Cierra has mixed settler and Red River Métis roots and is a member of the Manitoba Métis Federation.
